en.name: Pork floss
en.summary: Pork floss is pork simmered, shredded and dried — often fried — until it is light and fluffy, and it keeps because almost all the water is gone. A sealed commercial jar or pack runs about 12 months from purchase in the cupboard, and about 2–3 months refrigerated once opened. Both figures are read across from commercially dried jerky; no Taiwanese or Hong Kong authority publishes a home shelf life for 肉鬆.
en.pantry: A sealed commercial pack or jar is shelf-stable for about 12 months from purchase, because the drying has taken the water activity low enough that nothing grows. What ends it is not bacteria but the fat: heat and light turn it rancid, so keep the jar in a cool dark cupboard rather than on the shelf beside the stove, where most kitchens keep it. Always go by the printed date on the jar, which takes precedence over any general figure.
en.fridge: After opening, an airtight container in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below keeps it about 2–3 months — the cold slows the fat going rancid, and a sealed container keeps humidity out. Humidity is the real enemy of an opened jar: floss is hygroscopic and turns from fluffy to damp and clumpy very quickly in a Taiwanese summer. Always use a dry spoon or dry chopsticks, because one damp spoonful will mould the whole jar.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for pork floss and freezing it is not worth doing. The cupboard already gives you a year unopened and the fridge covers the months after that, and a freezer adds a real risk: condensation on the jar every time you take it out, which is exactly what wrecks a dried product. If you buy more than you can use, buy smaller jars instead.
spoilage: A rancid, old-oil smell — the usual way pork floss ends.
Colour gone dark or patchy rather than evenly golden-brown.
Clumping, dampness or a chewy rather than fluffy texture.
Any mould, which usually starts where a wet spoon touched it.
tips: Keep it away from the stove; heat costs you more shelf life than time does.
Use a dry spoon every single time and close the lid straight away.
Decant a big bag into a small airtight jar and refill it, rather than opening the whole bag.
Buy smaller jars if you only use it on congee at weekends.

faq.q: Does pork floss need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Not while it is sealed — a cool, dark cupboard for about 12 months from purchase. After opening, an airtight container in the fridge is the better home.

faq.q: How long does pork floss last after opening?
faq.a: About 2–3 months refrigerated in an airtight container. That figure is borrowed from commercially dried jerky rather than published for pork floss.
There is no timeline for it and no need. Condensation from a freezer is the fastest way to ruin a dried product.

faq.q: Why has my pork floss gone clumpy?
faq.a: It has absorbed moisture, usually from humid air or a damp spoon. Clumped floss is on its way to mould rather than merely stale.

zh.name: 肉鬆
zh.summary: 肉鬆是把豬肉煮軟、撕成細絲後乾炒或油酥到蓬鬆乾燥，靠的就是把水分幾乎全部趕走。未開封的市售罐裝或袋裝放櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 12 個月；開封後密封冷藏約 2～3 個月。這兩個數字都是比照「市售乾燥肉乾」讀過來的，台灣或香港都沒有單位替肉鬆公布家庭保存期限。
zh.pantry: 未開封的市售包裝從購買日起算約可常溫放 12 個月，因為乾燥已經把水活性壓得夠低，什麼都長不起來。終結它的通常不是細菌而是油脂：高溫和光線會讓油脂走油耗，所以請放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃，而不是大多數人習慣的爐台旁邊。罐子上的標示日期永遠優先於任何通則數字。
zh.fridge: 開封後放進密封容器、冷藏 4 °C 以下，約可放 2～3 個月——低溫延緩油脂氧化，密封擋住濕氣。對開封後的肉鬆來說，濕氣才是真正的敵人：它很會吸水，在台灣的夏天幾天就從蓬鬆變得受潮結塊。每次都要用乾燥的湯匙或筷子，因為只要一口濕的，整罐都會發霉。
zh.freezer: 肉鬆沒有冷凍期限，冷凍也不值得做。未開封放櫥櫃就有一年，開封後冷藏也涵蓋接下來的幾個月，而冷凍反而多一個風險：每次拿出來罐子都會結露，而那正是毀掉乾燥食品最快的方式。買太多的話，下次買小罐就好。
spoilage: 聞起來有油耗、陳油味——肉鬆最常見的結局。
顏色變深或深淺不均，而不是均勻的金褐色。
結塊、受潮，口感變得韌而不蓬鬆。
長霉，通常從沾過濕湯匙的位置開始。
tips: 遠離爐火；高溫奪走的壽命比時間還多。
每一次都用乾湯匙，用完立刻蓋緊。
大包裝分裝到小密封罐，用完再補，不要整包一直開。
如果只有週末配稀飯才吃，就買小罐的。

faq.a: 未開封不用，放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 12 個月。開封後改放密封容器冷藏比較好。

faq.q: 肉鬆開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封容器冷藏約 2～3 個月。這個數字借自市售乾燥肉乾，不是專為肉鬆公布的。
沒有對應期限，也沒有必要。冷凍庫拿進拿出的結露，是毀掉乾貨最快的方式。
它吸了水氣，通常來自潮濕空氣或沾濕的湯匙。結塊的肉鬆不只是不脆，而是正在往發霉的路上走。
